findings.title: Core model models/mel/Network.py (MYNET) is absent; nothing runs
findings.claim: fscil_trainer.py imports MYNET from a sibling module models/mel/Network.py and instantiates it at line 30 (self.model = MYNET(self.args)), but no Network.py (or any definition of MYNET) exists anywhere in the repo — models/mel/ contains only fscil_trainer.py and helper.py. A recursive grep for MYNET/Network finds only these two import/use sites.
findings.concern: The entire proposed model — the ResNet-12 wrapper, the meta-category vector m (referenced as model.module.attention), the mask-generation conv g_phi (Eq. 5), the transformation block h_phi (Eq. 10), the classifiers fc/part_fc, update_fc, encode1, and the forward pass producing (logits1, logits2, x1, part) — is missing, so the code cannot run and no result (Tables 1–6, Figs 3–9) is reproducible or traceable.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add models/mel/Network.py defining MYNET, or confirm which file defines the model and how logits1/logits2 (S_high/S_low) and the meta-category vector are constructed.
findings.reason: fscil_trainer.py line 7 has exactly 'from .Network import MYNET'; models/mel/ contains only fscil_trainer.py and helper.py; a recursive find confirms no Network.py exists anywhere in the repo.

findings.title: Dataset loaders for CUB200, Stanford Cars, FGVCAircraft are absent (only Stanford Dogs present)
findings.quote:
if args.dataset == 'cub200':
    import dataloader.cub200.cub200 as Dataset
findings.claim: set_up_datasets imports dataloader.cub200.cub200 (line 7), dataloader.StanfordCar.StanfordCar (line 24), and dataloader.Aircraft.Aircraft (line 32), but dataloader/ contains only the StanfordDog package (StanfordDog.py + autoaugment.py); the cub200/, StanfordCar/, and Aircraft/ loader modules do not exist. Selecting any of those three datasets raises ModuleNotFoundError at set_up_datasets.
findings.concern: Three of the four benchmark datasets cannot be loaded, so the CUB200 / Stanford Cars / FGVCAircraft columns of Table 1 and all of Tables 3, 5, 6 and Figure 3(a,c,d) are unreproducible from this repo.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add the cub200, StanfordCar, and Aircraft dataloader modules (the paper reports results on all four datasets).
findings.reason: data_utils.py lines 6-7 contain the cub200 import exactly as quoted; dataloader/ directory contains only StanfordDog/; cub200/, StanfordCar/, Aircraft/ subdirectories are absent.

findings.title: No dependency spec; helper.py hard-imports torch_dct (unlisted, never used)
findings.claim: helper.py (imported by fscil_trainer -> train.py) unconditionally imports the third-party package torch_dct at module load, yet dct is never referenced anywhere (grep for 'dct.' returns nothing). The repo ships no requirements.txt / environment.yml / setup.py, so torch, torchvision, tqdm, and torch_dct are neither pinned nor listed.
findings.concern: Running train.py fails with ModuleNotFoundError unless torch_dct is installed even though it serves no purpose, and with no dependency manifest the environment cannot be rebuilt to the versions used for the paper's numbers.
findings.resolution: Authors: remove the unused torch_dct import and add a pinned requirements.txt (torch/torchvision/tqdm/etc. versions).
findings.paper_ref: Checklist Q5 (open access to code); Appendix A.3
findings.reason: helper.py line 5 has 'import torch_dct as dct' exactly as quoted; grep for 'dct.' across the repo returns no hits; no requirements.txt, environment.yml, or setup.py exists in the repo root.

findings.title: Incremental few-shot TRAIN set is drawn from test.csv and overlaps the eval test set
findings.quote:
def SelectfromTxt(self, data2label, index_path):
    index = [x.strip().split('/')[2] for x in open(index_path, 'r').readlines()]
    target_by_class = {}
    for name in index:
        img_path = os.path.join(self.IMAGE_PATH, name)
        target_by_class[name.split('_')[0]] = data2label[img_path]

    csv_path = osp.join(self.SPLIT_PATH, 'test.csv')
    lines = [x.strip() for x in open(csv_path, 'r').readlines()][1:]
    data_tmp = []
    targets_tmp = []
    for class_name, target in target_by_class.items():
        names = [line.split(';')[0] for line in lines
                 if line.split(';')[0].split('_')[0] == class_name][:5]
        for name in names:
            data_tmp.append(os.path.join(self.IMAGE_PATH, name))
            targets_tmp.append(target)

    return data_tmp, targets_tmp
findings.claim: SelectfromTxt (the incremental-session training loader, called by get_new_dataloader for sessions >= 1) uses the session_N.txt few-shot list only to recover the set of novel-class wnids, then selects the first 5 images per class from test.csv (line 105) as the training data. _audit_code/check_incremental_leakage.py confirms on the shipped files: train.csv (8200) and test.csv (12380) are disjoint; for session_2..session_8 the intended few-shot images are all in train.csv, yet all 175 loaded training images (25 per session) come from test.csv and none from train.csv, and train/test wnid ordering is identical so labels align.
findings.concern: Every incremental novel class is trained (prototype in update_fc and the meta-category evolution in Eq. 9) on images that are themselves in the evaluation test set, so all incremental-session and novel-class accuracies — the paper's central FSCIL claim — are inflated by direct train/test leakage.
findings.resolution: Authors: SelectfromTxt should load the exact few-shot images listed in session_N.txt (which live in train.csv), not 5 images per class from test.csv; please re-run Stanford Dogs after fixing the source split and report the change.
findings.reason: Code at lines 98-116 matches the quote exactly; check_script ran successfully and confirmed: train.csv=8200, test.csv=12380, train∩test=0; all 175 incremental training images (25 per session across sessions 2-8) are drawn from test.csv, 0 from train.csv.

findings.topic: hyperparameter tuning / model selection on test
findings.title: Base checkpoint (and reported base accuracy) selected by best TEST accuracy
findings.quote:
tsl, tsa = test(self.model, testloader, epoch, args, session)

# save better model
if (tsa * 100) >= self.trlog['max_acc'][session]:
    self.trlog['max_acc'][session] = float('%.3f' % (tsa * 100))
    self.trlog['max_acc_epoch'] = epoch
    save_model_dir = os.path.join(args.save_path, 'session' + str(session) + '_max_acc.pth')
    torch.save(dict(params=self.model.state_dict()), save_model_dir)
    self.best_model_dict = deepcopy(self.model.state_dict())
findings.claim: During the 400-epoch base session the model is evaluated on the test loader every epoch, and the checkpoint kept (best_model_dict) plus the reported max_acc[0] is the epoch with the highest TEST accuracy. There is no separate validation split; testloader is built from test.csv (get_base_dataloader) and is the same set that is reported. best_model_dict is then carried into every incremental session (load_state_dict at line 62).
findings.concern: Selecting the checkpoint/epoch by test-set accuracy biases the reported base-session number upward and propagates an optimistically-selected backbone into all incremental sessions; the reported accuracies are a max over 400 epochs of test performance rather than a held-out estimate.
findings.resolution: Authors: select the checkpoint on a held-out validation split (not the test set) and report the resulting accuracies; confirm whether baselines were selected the same way.
findings.reason: fscil_trainer.py lines 71-79 match the quote exactly; test() is called on testloader every epoch and best_model_dict is updated when tsa (test accuracy) is the new maximum — no validation split is used.

findings.title: Base optimizer excludes module.encoder.* — backbone may never train (needs missing MYNET to confirm)
findings.quote:
excluded = set()
excluded.add('module.attention')

params = [
    param
    for name, param in model.named_parameters()
    if name not in excluded and not name.startswith('module.encoder.')
]

optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(
    [{'params': params, 'lr': args.lr_base},
     {'params': model.module.attention, 'lr': args.lr_base / 10}],
    momentum=args.momentum, nesterov=True,
    weight_decay=args.decay)
findings.claim: get_optimizer builds the base-session SGD with two param groups: `params` (every parameter EXCEPT module.attention and EXCEPT anything whose name starts with 'module.encoder.') and module.attention. Any parameter named module.encoder.* is therefore in no group and receives no gradient step. This is the only optimizer used by base_train.
findings.concern: If module.encoder is the from-scratch ResNet-12 backbone (models/resnet12_encoder.py; replace_base_fc also uses a mode='encoder'), then under the documented command (no -model_dir, random init) the backbone is never updated and stays at Kaiming random init, which cannot yield the reported ~65% base accuracy — contradicting the paper's core claim of evolving/trained fine-grained feature extraction. I cannot confirm module.encoder is that backbone because MYNET (Network.py) is missing, so this is filed as a question.
findings.resolution: Authors: confirm whether module.encoder is the trainable ResNet-12 backbone and, if so, why it is excluded from the base optimizer (is it intended to be pretrained/frozen, and if so from which checkpoint?).
findings.reason: utils.py lines 209-222 match the quote exactly; the filter 'not name.startswith("module.encoder.")' is confirmed present, placing all module.encoder.* parameters in no optimizer group; the question status is appropriate because MYNET is absent so encoder identity cannot be confirmed.

findings.title: Prose 'AccAvg 1.21% higher than CLOSER on CUB200' disagrees with Table 1 (gap = 1.48)
findings.quote: our method achieves a 1.21% higher average accuracy (AccAvg) than CLOSER on the CUB200
findings.claim: Table 1 (and per-session Table 3, whose rows I re-averaged: Ours = 45.44, CLOSER = 43.95) gives a CUB200 AccAvg gap of 45.44 - 43.95 = 1.48/1.49, not 1.21. The companion AccT claim in the same sentence (4.26%) matches exactly (36.00 - 31.74 = 4.26), so the 1.21 figure is the inconsistent one.
findings.concern: Minor arithmetic inconsistency between the prose and the paper's own tables; it does not change the ranking (Ours still leads on CUB200), but the stated margin is understated.
findings.resolution: Authors: correct the CUB200 AccAvg margin (should be ~1.48-1.49%) or clarify what '1.21%' refers to.
findings.reason: Quote found at paper_text.txt line 753; Table 3 re-average confirms CLOSER=43.95, Ours=45.44, gap=1.48, not 1.21; AccT gap 36.00-31.74=4.26 matches prose correctly, confirming the 1.21 value is the erroneous one.
